author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell begins by questioning where the real threat to ordinary people comes from, arguing that changing political leaders does not necessarily change the deeper systems of power beneath them. He then shifts the conversation away from politics entirely, saying that breaking free begins with a spiritual decision: recognizing that this life and this physical form are temporary.

From there, Russell turns to Abraham and Isaac. He describes Abraham’s faith that even if Isaac died, God had the power to raise him from the dead because of the promise already made to him. The story then becomes a parallel to Christ: in Russell’s telling, humanity ultimately does not have to provide the sacrifice because God gives His own Son instead.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reflects on the old phrase about there being “no atheists on a sinking ship” and what happens when the comforts of ordinary life suddenly stop feeling sufficient. When death or crisis becomes real, he suggests, people begin reaching beyond the material world for a different kind of reality.

He then describes the feeling that something about the world simply isn’t working — and asks whether drugs, sex, fame, money or other material pleasures can ever be transformed into the deeper, sanctifying experience people may actually be searching for. His conclusion is that they cannot.

The deeper question is whether crisis creates that spiritual realization — or simply reveals something that was already there.
